problem: Diffusion-based visual navigation planners generate diverse trajectory candidates, but selection relies on analytic critics with hand-tuned, globally fixed clearance margins. These are either too conservative (detours, timeouts) or too permissive (risky near-boundary shortcuts under perception bias).
motivation: Required clearance depends on context: local clutter, maneuver demands and perception reliability. The same measured distance can be safe in one situation and risky in another. A selector should therefore learn an adaptive safe distance and trade safety against efficiency per scene.
key_idea: Learn a context-conditioned safety critic with a per-waypoint adaptive clearance budget (safety + gated efficiency + balance terms) using privileged ESDF in a teacher, then distill it into an RGB-D-only selector that ranks diffusion trajectory proposals.
insight: The three critic terms are complementary. Removing V_efficient keeps SR at 0.707 but drops SPL to 0.468 (over-conservative detours). Removing V_balance drops SR to 0.633 (SPL 0.585), because the budget loses its anchor to realized clearance. Removing V_safe gives SR 0.690. The adaptive margin also lets the robot pass a DoN=0.75 gap that a fixed 0.5 m NavDP margin refuses, while a 0.1 m floor prevents collapse at DoN=0.90.
method: Diffusion generator: NavDP/T-diff style transformer encoder on RGB-D plus optional goal token, DDPM U-Net denoiser with SNR-weighted loss, sampling K=16 trajectories of ego-motion offsets
Context-conditioned margin head: d_min,j = 0.1 m + softplus(MLP(local ESDF clearance, ESDF gradient magnitude, step index j/T)), giving a time-varying safety budget
Safety term V_safe: count of waypoints violating d_min,j plus a control-barrier-function residual penalty (rho=0.1) relative to the fixed floor
Efficiency term V_efficient: second-difference smoothness penalty plus a detour-ratio hinge (path length / chord) gated by a sigmoid of (d_j - d_min,j) so shortcuts near obstacles are not rewarded
Balance term V_balance: -psi * sum (d_j - d_min,j)^2, which anchors the budget to realized ESDF clearance and prevents margin collapse

Teacher training: adversarial logistic discriminator D=sigmoid(a V + b) separates A*+spline expert paths from ESDF-conditioned non-expert A* paths (randomized edge costs) under matched start/goal; penalty weights (softplus-reparameterized) and margin head are learned
Student selector: RGB-D plus trajectory-token network regresses the teacher scores (MSE, stopgrad) on a mix of expert and diffusion-generated candidates, so inference needs no ESDF

setting.backbone: Diffusion transformer/U-Net generator (NavDP-style) + learned critic MLP teacher + RGB-D/trajectory-token student selector, all trained
setting.training_data: Simulated 3D scene data (HM3D-converted): A*+cubic-spline paths with paired RGB-D, five sliding windows per trajectory resampled to T=24 waypoints, ESDF from voxel maps, plus synthetic non-expert A* trajectories
setting.action_space: predicted trajectory waypoints (ego-motion offsets dx, dz, dtheta) converted to velocity commands
setting.privileged: ESDF geometry used only offline for teacher training; none at test time

numbers.eval_set_note: 300 episodes, identical episode set for all methods; 500-step timeout
numbers.evidence: Table 1 'Results for Three Simulation Tests', HM3D: 235/300, 0.783, 0.611

numbers.eval_set_note: 300 episodes, identical episode set for all methods

numbers.extra: trained on HM3D, tested on MP3D

numbers.eval_set_note: 10 episodes per scene; corridor / apartment / lab
numbers.extra: real Unitree G1 with RealSense D435i; no task-specific tuning

numbers_note: SR and SPL are printed as 0-1 decimals and converted to 0-100. Splits are not named officially; 'val' is assumed for the 300 sampled episodes.
results: On 300 PointGoal episodes the method reaches SR 0.783 / SPL 0.611 on HM3D, beating NavDP (0.710 / 0.529) and iPlanner, and SR 0.680 on MP3D vs NavDP 0.627. Under HM3D->MP3D transfer it reaches SR 0.597 / SPL 0.465 (best baseline SR: iPlanner 0.570). On a real G1 humanoid it succeeds in 28/30 episodes vs NavDP's 25/30, and in the hard lab 8/10 vs 6/10.
limitations: Evaluated only on PointGoal with small sample sizes (300 sim episodes, 10 real episodes per scene) and few baselines
Requires ESDF/privileged geometry and a two-stage pipeline in training; the fixed 0.1 m floor and other hyperparameters (rho, K) are hand-set
Gains over NavDP are modest, and the Panel A ESDF sensitivity results are non-monotone (SR 0.740-0.807)
